questions.explanation: HTML stands for Hyper Text Markup Language, the standard markup language for creating web pages.

questions.text: Which tag is used to create a hyperlink?
questions.explanation: The `<a>` (anchor) tag is used to define a hyperlink.

questions.text: Which element is used to define the title of a document?
questions.explanation: The `<title>` tag defines the title of the document, shown in the browser tab.

questions.text: What is the purpose of the 'alt' attribute for images?
options: To provide alternative text for screen readers
To link the image to another page
questions.explanation: The `alt` attribute provides a text description of an image for accessibility and when the image cannot be loaded.

questions.text: Which tag is used for an unordered list?
questions.explanation: The `<ul>` tag defines an unordered (bulleted) list.

questions.text: How do you create a line break in HTML?
questions.explanation:
The `
` tag is used for a single line break.

questions.text: Which tag is used to define a table row?
questions.explanation: The `<tr>` tag defines a row in an HTML table.

questions.text: Which HTML element is used for the largest heading?
questions.explanation: HTML headings range from `<h1>` (largest/most important) to `<h6>` (smallest).

questions.text: What is the correct tag for a footer?
questions.explanation: The `<footer>` tag is a semantic element used for the footer of a document or section.

questions.text: Which attribute is used to uniquely identify an element?
questions.explanation: The `id` attribute provides a unique identifier for an HTML element within a page.
`<div>` is a block-level element, used for grouping large sections of content and starts on a new line. `<span>` is an inline element, used for grouping small portions of text within a line.

questions.text: Why is the `<!DOCTYPE html>` declaration important?
questions.explanation: It tells the browser that the document is an HTML5 document. This ensures that the browser parses the page in 'standards mode' rather than 'quirks mode'.

questions.text: What are the benefits of using semantic HTML elements?
questions.explanation: Semantic elements improve accessibility for screen reader users, make the code more readable for developers, and help search engines (SEO) better understand the content of the page.

questions.text: Describe the difference between an absolute and a relative URL in an anchor tag.
questions.explanation: An absolute URL contains the full address (including protocol like https://), pointing to a specific location on the web. A relative URL points to a file relative to the current page (e.g., 'about.html').

questions.text: How do you add a comment in HTML code?
questions.explanation: Comments in HTML are written using the syntax `<!-- Comment goes here -->`. They are not visible in the browser but can be seen in the source code.
